metadata.description: A physical place resources sit in — a site, a room, a rack, a bench — nesting into a containment hierarchy. A Base by the Base test (CLS-002): Redfish Location and Placement abstract over every granularity the same way for every facility provider, so a location of a given kind is one deliverable any of them reports or realizes. Power is not here: each host carries its own edge to the PowerFeed it draws from, which can differ within one rack.

kind.description: The granularity: site, room, rack, bench, slot.

position.description: Placement within the parent (rack units U20-U21, a grid cell).

occupant_count.description: DERIVED — a count of the resources whose location edge resolves to this Location; the graph is the source (compute-never-store: a stored copy drifts the moment a resource moves). How many resources are currently located in this place.

relationships.name: within
relationships.description: The parent place this location nests inside (bench within room within site).

adopts.role: physical-placement vocabulary (site/rack/row/unit, coordinates) — referenced, not restated

context.purpose: Names a physical place — site, room, rack, bench — that resources sit in, nesting into a containment hierarchy.
context.plain_description: A physical place, at whatever granularity is useful: a site contains rooms, a room contains racks, a rack has positions. Resources declare where they physically sit by referencing a location; location-scoped concerns like cooling or a shared uplink attach at the right level of the hierarchy. Power is not carried here — each host declares its own power-feed edges, because two hosts in one rack can draw from different feeds.
use_when: You need to record where equipment physically is, down to a rack position.
You need placement intent for a VM or workload to select among existing places.
not_for: Failure or locality domains for placement constraints (zone, power domain, rack-as-failure-domain) — that is Topology: put resources IN Locations, constrain placement AGAINST Topology.
Power sources — PowerFeed, referenced per host, not per location.
works_with: Location — the parent place this one nests inside.
Machine.BareMetalHost — the equipment that declares its location.
Topology — the failure-domain view of the same physical reality.
